Rashi on Nedarim 60b:1:1.hebrew: אי הכי ליגזור יום אחד - דליהוי אסור עד שתחשך למחר משום היום, דאי אמרת עד מעת לעת אסור ותו לא, אתו למישרי נמי — כי עמד בשחרית ואמר היום, אתי למישתי בחצי היום, והוא אסור עד שתחשך:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:1:1.english: If so, let us decree [concerning] "one day" - That he should be forbidden until it grows dark tomorrow, because of [the case of] "today." For if you say [that he is] forbidden [only] for a twenty-four-hour period and no more, they will come to permit [it] also — when one rose in the morning and said "today," he will come to drink in the middle of the day, whereas he is [actually] forbidden until it grows dark.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:2:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רב יוסף היום ביום אחד מיחלף - דאי שרית היום לכשתחשך בלא שאלה, מיחלף ואתי למישרי יום אחד משתחשך, דסבר יצא אותו היום שנדר בו כמו כן; והוא אינו מותר אלא מעת לעת:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:2:1.english: Rav Yosef said to him: "Today" is interchanged with "one day" - For if you permit [a vow of] "today" when night falls without [requiring] a request [for absolution], it will be confused [with it] and one will come to permit [a vow of] "one day" once night falls, because he thinks that the day on which he vowed has likewise ended; whereas it is not permitted except [after] a twenty-four-hour period.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:2:2.hebrew: יום אחד בהיום לא מיחלף - דלא אשור לשתות למחר עד הלילה, דלא אתי למישרי בהיום מחצי יום ואילך, דליכא למיחש להכי, דהכא לא גמר היום עדיין ומידע ידיע דאסור כל היום. משום האי טעמא נמי לא מצרכינן שאלה לסוף מעת לעת, דלא אתו למישרי מהיום מחצי יום ואילך, דליכא למיחש בהכי, כדאמרינן: הכא לא גמר עדיין היום, ומידע ידיע דאסור בכל היום:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:2:2.english: [A vow for] one day is not interchanged with [a vow for] today - For he is not forbidden to drink tomorrow until nightfall, as he will not come to permit [himself to drink] in [a vow for] "today" from midday onwards, since there is no need to be concerned about this — as here the day has not yet ended, and it is well known that he is forbidden [for] the entire day. For this same reason as well, we do not require absolution [by a sage] at the end of the twenty-four hour period, for people will not come to permit [themselves] in [a vow for] "today" from midday onwards, since there is no need to be concerned about this — as we said, here the day has not yet ended, and it is well known that he is forbidden for the entire day.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:3:1.hebrew: כמאן אזלא - הא שמעתתא דאמר רב ירמיה דצריך שאלה לחכם, שאין ניתר ע"פ עצמו כלל, דמחמרינן עליה כמאן דלא עבד שפיר:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:3:1.english: In accordance with whom does [it] go - This teaching that Rav Yirmeya said, that he requires inquiry to a sage, for it is not permitted on his own word at all, since we are stringent upon him as one who did not act properly.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:3:2.hebrew: כרבי נתן וכו' - הילכך צריך שאלה לחכם, הואיל ועבד איסורא, דמחמרינן עליה ואין מראין לו שקיים נדרו מעצמו אלא כשיתירו לו את נדרו, ולא משום גזירה — דרבינא לא סבירא ליה דרב יוסף. וכל היכא דאיכא לאוקומי ביה שאלה, מצריכינן ליה שאלה, כגון הכא דאמר היום, דאיכא למימר מעת לעת קאמר; הילכך לכשתחשך צריך שאלה לחכם. אבל כי אמר כבת וכולה מתניתין, דליכא לאוקומי בהו שאלה, דודאי לא משמע טפי, אין צריך שאלה:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:3:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Natan, etc. - Therefore, he requires an inquiry to a sage, since he committed a transgression [by vowing]; for we are stringent with him and do not give him the impression that he has fulfilled his vow on his own, unless they [the sages] permit his vow for him — and not because of a [rabbinic] decree, for Ravina does not agree with [the view of] Rav Yosef. And wherever it is possible to apply [the requirement of] an inquiry to it, we require an inquiry of him — such as here, where he said "today," since one can say that he meant a twenty-four-hour period; therefore, when it becomes dark, he requires an inquiry to a sage. However, when he said "this week" [text: כבת, for שבת] and all [the other cases in] the Mishnah, where it is not possible to apply [a requirement of] an inquiry to them — because [the wording] certainly does not imply any longer — he does not require an inquiry.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:4:1.english: He said the days of the week - [The] days of the week, and not of Shabbat itself.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:5:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דיום ראש חדש נמי אסור, שהרי יום ראש חדש נמנה לחדש זה הנכנס:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:5:1.english: [Isn't it] obvious - That the day of Rosh Chodesh is also forbidden, for the day of Rosh Chodesh is counted as part of this entering month.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:5:2.hebrew: כי איצטריך - למיתני במתניתין לחדש חסר, בחדש שהוא שני ימים ראש חדש, ויום ראשון של ראש חדש משלים לחדש מלא זה שעבר, וזה הנכנס חסר הוא. והוא נדר ביום ראשון של ר"ח:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:5:2.english: When it was necessary - to teach [this] in the Mishnah, [it was] for a deficient month, in [the case of] a month that has two days of Rosh Chodesh, where the first day of Rosh Chodesh completes this full month that has passed, and this incoming [month] is deficient. And he took the vow on the first day of Rosh Chodesh.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:6:1.english: [It] is of the previous month - And [it] should not be forbidden on it.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:6:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - אפילו הכי, כיון דקרו ליה ריש ירחא, אסור ביה נמי:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:6:2.english: [The Gemara] teaches us - Even so, since people call it the beginning of the month, he is forbidden during it as well.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:8:1.hebrew: דיניה כהיום - כאילו אמר היום לחוד, ומותר לכשתחשך:
Rashi on Nedarim 60b:8:1.english: [What is] his law? [Is it] as "today" - [Meaning,] as if he said "today" alone, and he is permitted [to drink wine] once it grows dark.

Rashi on Nedarim 60b:8:2.english: Or as "one day" - And he is prohibited for a twenty-four-hour period.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:10:1.english: Rather, no [inference] is to be learned from this [mishna] - For we do not know which [clause] is exact, whether the first clause or the latter clause.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:11:1.hebrew: ת"ש קונם יין שאני טועם השנה אסור בה עד סופה - ולא מיום ליום, הילכך עד ראש השנה; ואף כי נתעברה, כל השנה עד סופה נקראת משנה זו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:11:1.english: Come [and] hear: "Konam [is] wine that I taste this year" — he is prohibited from it until its end - and not from day to day; therefore, [he is prohibited] until Rosh Hashanah, and even if it was intercalated, the entire year until its end is considered [part] of this year.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:11:2.english: Why does [the Tanna] need [to state it] - [For] it is obvious that he is prohibited in it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:3:1.hebrew: אמר רבינא כו' כר' נתן - וקנסא קנסינן ליה אף כי קיים נדרו עד שישאל לחכם. ונראה דרבינא מוסיף על טעם דרב יוסף משום גזירה, דבשאר נדרים לא קנסינן לשאול לחכם לאחר שנתקיימו, אלא אית ליה טעמא דנדרים דגזרינן לעיל, וקאמר דבהך טעמא דגזרי' לא סגי אם לא מטעם דקנסינן ליה כר' נתן, שעבר על מה שקיימו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:3:1.english: Ravina said, etc., in accordance with Rabbi Natan - And we penalize him, even though he has fulfilled his vow, [that he remains prohibited] until he consults a sage. And it appears that Ravina is adding to Rav Yosef's reason [based] on a decree, for with other vows we do not penalize [someone by requiring him] to consult a sage after they have been fulfilled; rather, he accepts the reason regarding [the] vows about which we enacted a decree above, and he is saying that this reason of the decree does not suffice without the reason that we penalize him in accordance with Rabbi Natan, since he transgressed by fulfilling it:

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:4:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דאסור לשבת הבאה, דבשבוע שעבר היא. מהו דתימא: יומא דשבת לא אסר עצמו, אלא בימי המעשה שבשבוע, ולא נתכוין לאסור בשבת — קמ"ל. ולפירוש שני דמתני', פריך: "פשיטא", כיון דקאי בשבת, דאסור בו! ומשני: מהו דתימא דיומי שבוע העתידין לבא קאמר, ולא יום השבת עצמו — קמ"ל דכיון דקאי בשבת, אמרינן דאף בשבת נדר. ונ"ל דהטעם לפי שלשון בני אדם לקרות השבוע "שבת", וא"כ לשבוע הבא הוא מתכוין, ולא לשבת לבד; ומכל מקום, כיון שעומד בשבת, אמר שדעתו גם לשבת, כדי שלא יהיה ספק בנדרו, ושיחול משעה שנדר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:4:1.english: "Isn't it obvious" - that he is prohibited for the coming Shabbat, since it is [part] of the week that has passed [i.e., the current week]? Lest you say [that on] the day of Shabbat he did not prohibit himself, [but] only on the weekdays of the week, and he did not intend to prohibit [himself] on Shabbat — it teaches us [otherwise]. And according to the second explanation of the Mishnah, [the Gemara] asks: "Isn't it obvious," since he is standing on Shabbat, that he is prohibited on it! And [the Gemara] answers: Lest you say that he means the days of the week that are yet to come, and not the day of Shabbat itself — it teaches us that since he is standing on Shabbat, we say that he also vowed regarding Shabbat. And it seems to me that the reason is because it is the usage of people to call the week "Shabbat," and if so, he intends [his vow] for the coming week, and not for Shabbat alone; nevertheless, since he is standing on Shabbat, he says [i.e., means] that his intention is also for Shabbat, so that there will be no doubt regarding his vow, and so that it will take effect from the moment he vowed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:5:1.hebrew: חדש זה פשיטא - דראש חדש נידון בחדש הבא ומותר בו? כי איצטריך לחדש חסר — כלומר, נדר באמצע חדש מלא וחדש חסר אחריו, שר"ח שני ימים, ויום ראשון הוא להשלים יום של חדש שעבר, דקס"ד דאסור בו; קמ"ל דהא קרו אינשי ריש ירחא ליום ראשון של ר"ח, ובחודש הבא דיינינן ליה, שאינו מנוי בלשון בני אדם בחדש שעבר. ולפירוש אחר: פשיטא כיון דעומד בר"ח דאסור בו! לא צריכא אלא לחדש חסר שראש חדש שלו שני ימים, ונדר ביום ראשון ר"ח שעבר, ולא נתכוון אלא בימי של חדש שעבר; קמ"ל דקרו אינשי ריש ירחא ואינו נמנה בחדש שעבר, והילכך כי אמר "חדש זה" מיתסר ביה. וניחא טפי לישנא ד"חדש חסר" לפירוש אחרון. וכיון דקאמר דקרו ליה אינשי ריש ירחא, א"כ כשכותבין כתובה או שטרות ביום ראשון של ר"ח, כותבין "יום פלוני שהוא ראש חדש", ואין צריך לכתוב "יום שלשים"; דהכי משמע לקמן (נדרים סג -) דתנן: "עד ר"ח אדר [עד ר"ח אדר] הראשון", ומדמה בגמ' הך ברייתא דשטרות [לנדרים], אלמא דין שטרות כדין נדרים דלשון בני אדם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:5:1.english: "This month" — Isn't it obvious? - That Rosh Chodesh is judged as part of the next month and he is permitted [to benefit] on it? When was it necessary? For a deficient month — that is to say, he vowed in the middle of a full month and a deficient month follows it, where Rosh Chodesh is two days and the first day is to complete the [thirtieth] day of the previous month, so you might have thought that he is forbidden on it; [therefore] it teaches us that people call the first day of Rosh Chodesh "reish yarcha" [the New Moon], and we judge it as part of the next month, for in human parlance it is not counted in the previous month. And according to another explanation: Isn't it obvious, since he is standing on Rosh Chodesh [when he vows], that he is forbidden on it? It is only necessary for a deficient month whose Rosh Chodesh is two days, and he vowed on the first day of Rosh Chodesh [which belongs to] the previous [month], and he only intended the days of the previous month; [therefore] it teaches us that people call it "reish yarcha" and it is not counted in the previous month, and therefore when he says "this month," he is forbidden on it. And the wording "a deficient month" fits better according to the latter explanation. And since [the Gemara] says that people call it "reish yarcha," if so, when writing a ketubah or legal documents on the first day of Rosh Chodesh, one writes "such-and-such a day which is Rosh Chodesh," and there is no need to write "day thirty"; for so it is implied later (Nedarim 63a), where we learned in a Mishnah: "until Rosh Chodesh Adar [until Rosh Chodesh Adar] HaRishon," and the Gemara compares that baraita of documents [to vows] — thus, the law of documents is like the law of vows, [which follows] human parlance.

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:5:2.hebrew: פסק - ומיהו בגיטין טוב לכתוב שהוא יום שלשים לחדש טבת, וכן כתב רבינו תם בכתובת בתו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:5:2.english: Ruling - However, in bills of divorce [gittin], it is good to write that it is the thirtieth day of the month of Tevet, and so did Rabbeinu Tam write in his daughter's ketubah [marriage contract].

Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:8:1.hebrew: דיניה כהיום - ומותר משתחשך, או כיום אחד ואסור במעת לעת:
Tosafot on Nedarim 60b:8:1.english: His law [is] like "today" - and he is permitted once it grows dark, or like "one day" and he is prohibited for a twenty-four-hour period.
